$comment: TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-ASM-LABEL-SYMBOL-RENAME) — the GNU/Clang asm label (symbol rename) and the multi-declarator typedef, both runtime-observable in one exit code. SUPERSEDES the diagnostics-corpus file `asm_label_on_declaration.c`, which pinned the construct as a loud parse error and said in its own banner that the golden would change deliberately when the feature landed; the shapes that STAY rejected moved to `asm_label_invalid.c`. RED-ON-DISABLE: the label is what makes `entry` and `renamed_target` the same symbol — parse-and-ignore makes `entry` an undefined reference (loud link failure, not a wrong exit code), and mangling the label instead of replacing the mangling makes the Mach-O definition `_dss_c88_impl` while the reference asks for `dss_c88_impl` (also a loud link failure). The typedef arm is what forces all three aliases to bind: dropping declarators 2..N stops the program compiling.
